newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Twenty injured at Pakistan independence day rally.
newsitem.headline: Twenty injured at Pakistan independence day rally.

text.p: At least 20 people were injured on Thursday when a crowd stampeded at a rally to mark Pakistan's independence day, witnesses said.
Police fired in the air and spectators with batons while President Farooq Leghari and Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif were visiting the tomb of Pakistan's founder Mohammad Ali Jinnah.

Several government officials had to fight their way through crowds after the baton charge. A senior police officer said the crowd had attacked police while they were trying to protect school girls in colourful dresses who had been brought in to sing folk songs for Sharif.

But another official said the trouble among the crowd, estimated to number 20,000, had begun when Sharif had said people should be allowed to come forward. "Security is in the hands of God. Let the people come close," Sharif was quoted as saying.
The crowd then broke through police cordons and rushed towards the podium. Shrieks of women and children filled the air as dozens of people fell and were trampled underfoot.
Pakistan gained its independence from Britain on August 14, 1947.
